general_information.Description: This course is based on the first course in the CCNA curriculum. It introduces the network architectures, models, protocols, and components that enable communication among users, devices, applications, and data across modern computer networks and the Internet. Key topics include Ethernet fundamentals, IP addressing, basic network operations, and introductory network security. By the end of the course, students will be able to build and configure simple local area networks (LANs), develop appropriate IP addressing schemes, apply basic security measures, configure routers and switches, verify network connectivity, and troubleshoot common network problems. The course includes an individual Practical Examination (PE) that assesses each student’s ability to apply these skills independently. During the examination, students are required to design or complete a small network, calculate and configure IP addresses, perform basic router and switch configurations, secure network devices, verify connectivity, and identify and correct common configuration errors. The course is organized into a series of modules, each of which represents an integrated unit of learning. Every module includes instructional content, practical activities, and assessments aligned with a defined set of competencies. The scope and duration of each module vary according to the level of knowledge and practical skill required. Some modules provide foundational knowledge that supports later learning and prepares students for concepts covered in the CCNA certification examination, even where the foundational content is not assessed directly.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information - Students must complete all assignments on the Cisco Networking Academy (https://www.netacad.com/) with a result of at least 75%.
general_information.Tools: Baseline Equipment Bundle: - 2 x ISR4221/K9 Routers - 2 x WS-C2960+24TC-L Catalyst switches - 1 wireless router (generic brand) with WPA2 support - Ethernet patch cables - PCs - Internet connection for lab and study PCs - Optional equipment for connecting to a WLAN + 1 printer or integrated printer/scanner/copier for the class to share + Smartphones and tablets are desirable for use with the labs Software: - Cisco IOS versions: + Routers: Version 15.0 or higher, IP Base feature set + Switches: Version 15.0 or higher, lanbaseK9 feature set - Packet Tracer, the most recent version. - Open-source server software: + For various services and protocols, such as Telnet, SSH, HTTP, DHCP, FTP, TFTP, etc. - Tera Term source SSH client software for lab PCs. - Oracle VirtualBox, most recent version. - Wireshark, the most recent version.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Describe the evolution of network technologies and explain how layered protocols enable communication and support end-user applications.
Students use AI and digital tools to collaborate, design, and present small network projects. The approach blends dialogue-based assessment with self-directed learning.
Apply Ethernet and switching concepts to explain and configure technologies that support efficient and reliable data transfer.
Configure switches, routers, and end devices with IP addressing and security settings to establish basic network connectivity.
Explain how physical, data link, network, and transport layers interact to enable reliable and structured data communication.
Design and implement IPv4 and IPv6 addressing schemes by calculating subnets and applying efficient address configurations in networks.
Use diagnostic tools and techniques to test and troubleshoot network connectivity, including ICMP utilities and AI-assisted methods.
Implement basic security measures by applying device hardening and configuration techniques to protect network devices and communications.
Design and implement a small network topology with routers, switches, and end devices, considering performance and scalability.
Utilize AI tools to analyze, configure, monitor, and troubleshoot networks, enhancing learning, efficiency, and network management capabilities.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Interpret or complete a basic network topology. Calculate IPv4 subnets and assign IPv4 addresses correctly. onfigure basic IPv6 addressing when included in the approved PE blueprint. Configure switches, routers and end devices. Configure default gateways and router interfaces. Apply basic device security, including passwords, encrypted secrets, banners, SSH or login protection when required. Verify connectivity using show commands, ping, tracert/traceroute or equivalent utilities. Identify and correct common addressing, interface, gateway, VLAN, routing or security configuration errors.
assessments.Note: The PE question bank should contain multiple equivalent variants. Network numbers, host requirements, device names and planted configuration errors should be randomized to reduce copying while maintaining equivalent difficulty.
